summary: onsaleFull discards all evidence when any stage aborts — defer writeReport
description:
### Finding (TKT-125 measurement, 2026-07-27)

`writeReport(t, report)` is the **last statement** of `onsaleFull` (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go`). Every `generatorHealthy` check is a `t.Fatalf`, so a single aborted stage discards the whole accumulated `report` — including stages that completed cleanly minutes earlier.

This cost TKT-125 its COS: on a single-host setup the ceiling sweep's `sweep-600` stage trips the generator guard **every time** (3 runs of 3, on 4-9 client-side transport errors at 600 attempts/s), so no JSON was ever emitted, even though the `nfr-3000pm` stage the ticket actually needed had completed 9,000/9,000 clean. `finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms` exist only in that report, so they could not be recorded.

### Scope

`defer writeReport(t, report)` (or equivalent) so a partial run still emits what it measured. The report already carries per-stage entries appended as they complete, so partial output is meaningful, not misleading — but consider marking the report `partial: true` so a reader cannot mistake an aborted run for a complete one.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An `onsaleFull` run whose sweep aborts still writes `ONSALE_REPORT` containing every completed stage
- [ ] The report distinguishes complete from partial runs
- [ ] TKT-125's missing `finalize_p99_ms` / `confirm_p99_ms` are obtainable by re-running the two arms
- [ ] `make check` green

objective.note: An aborted stage discards every stage that already completed; TKT-125 lost finalize_p99_ms/confirm_p99_ms to it.

scope.note: IN: defer writeReport + a partial marker in smoke/onsale_load_test.go. OUT: re-running the ceiling sweep to harvest TKT-125s numbers, and any change to the generatorHealthy guard itself.

uncertainties.note: Only whether a partial report can mislead a reader — closed by the partial marker (AC 2). t.Fatalf runs deferred functions, so defer is sufficient; no goroutine-exit path in onsaleFull bypasses it.

dependencies.note: None. smoke/onsale_load_test.go is untouched by anything in flight.

approach.note: defer writeReport(t, report) at the top of onsaleFull (currently the last statement, :519) + report.partial set true unless the run reaches the end.

first_slice.note: One function, one defer, one field. Whole ticket is the slice.

success.note: AC 3 resolved to mechanism-only (see readiness comment) — an injected abort proves the completed stages survive; harvesting TKT-125s numbers is a separate run, not this diff.

context_memo.note: No ADR governs the smoke load harness reporting format — checked all of docs/adr/ at HEAD. ADR-030 is the catalog coverage gate, not this. Recorded as a finding, not an omission.

From TKT-125's measurement. The one-line fix was deliberately **not** taken in TKT-125 because that ticket's plan explicitly recorded that `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` would not be modified — filing rather than widening scope. See `docs/evidence/TKT-125/README.md` § Known gap.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### DoR — 8/8 (1 deferred). Shaped 2026-07-28.

**Decision taken at shaping (owner call, delegated):** AC 3 is **mechanism-only**. The ticket
delivers "a partial report survives an aborted sweep"; it does **not** require re-running the
ceiling sweep to actually record TKT-125's `finalize_p99_ms` / `confirm_p99_ms`. Reason: on a
single-host setup `sweep-600` trips the generator guard every time (3/3 runs), so binding this
diff to a green full run binds it to a host it cannot have. Rewrite AC 3 as: *an `onsaleFull`
run aborted at `sweep-600` writes a report containing the `nfr-3000pm` stage's
`finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms`* — provable by an injected abort in seconds.

`context_memo` is `deferred`, not skipped: no ADR governs the load harness's reporting. Checked
docs/adr/ at HEAD; the nearest candidate (ADR-030) is the catalog coverage gate.

**Verdict: READY.** `risk:low` stands — one `defer`, one bool, no source outside `smoke/`.

---

### ⚠️ PROCESS WAIVER — this ticket runs **gateless**, by owner instruction

Recorded here so the board history shows what was and was not human-checked:

| 2 — plan approval | human moves Planning → Building | **waived.** Agent resolves open decisions itself: prefer the plan-critique's recommendation; absent one, the most reversible option. Every self-made decision is recorded in `kind=plan-final`. (Also nominally skipped anyway by `risk:low`.) |

**Unchanged and non-negotiable for this run:** `config.models` routing with no substitutions

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — authored by **gpt-5.6-sol** (`config.models.plan`), effort high, read-only

Run via the codex companion `task` command, no `--write`. Verbatim below; critique follows in
`kind=plan-final`.

---

## DoD

- `onsaleFull` writes `ONSALE_REPORT` from a deferred path whenever reporting has begun, including after `t.Fatalf`.
- An aborted run contains every previously accepted stage; specifically, `nfr-3000pm` retains `finalize_p99_ms` and `confirm_p99_ms`.
- Every new report explicitly contains `"partial": true` after an abort and `"partial": false` after normal completion.
- The aborting `sweep-600` stage remains excluded because `generatorHealthy` runs before its append (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go:474-480`); invalid generator evidence must not be published.
- `generatorHealthy` is unchanged.
- The normal `make check` gate passes. No real ceiling sweep is run for this ticket.

## Plan

1. Add `Partial bool \`json:"partial"\`` to `loadtest.Report` at `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:312-329`. Do not use `omitempty`, so complete reports explicitly serialize `false`.

2. Add a small reporting-lifecycle helper near `writeReport` (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go:250-263`) that:

   - Sets `report.Partial = true`.
   - Defers `writeReport(t, report)`.
   - Invokes the supplied profile body synchronously.
   - Sets `report.Partial = false` only after that body returns normally.

   Wrap the existing `onsaleFull` body with this helper. Keep the stage order and `generatorHealthy` closure (`:409-418`) unchanged. The NFR report is already appended before the sweep (`:430-441`), and its percentile fields originate at `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:289-304`.

3. Apply the same helper to `onsaleGate`, replacing its terminal write at `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:391`. It has the identical loss mode after appending stages (`:303-342`) and shares the same report schema; profile-dependent semantics would be surprising.

4. Add the regression tests described below, then run `make check`.

## Test seam

Add `smoke/onsale_load_report_test.go` with the `smoke` build tag.

- Complete-path test: set `ONSALE_REPORT` to `t.TempDir()`, invoke the reporting helper with a callback that returns normally, parse the JSON, and assert the `partial` key is present and `false`.
- Abort-path test: execute the current test binary as a subprocess with an environment sentinel and temporary `ONSALE_REPORT`. In child mode, invoke the same reporting helper; append a synthetic `nfr-3000pm` `StageReport` with distinct `FinalizeP99Ms` and `ConfirmP99Ms`, then call `t.Fatalf("injected abort at sweep-600")`.
- The parent must assert:

  - The subprocess exits non-zero for the expected injected diagnostic.
  - The JSON file exists and parses.
  - `partial` is explicitly `true`.
  - `nfr-3000pm` exists with the exact injected finalize/confirm p99 values.

The subprocess is necessary because an expected `t.Fatal` cannot be neutralized by a subtest: it permanently fails its parent test. The deferred writer still receives a real `*testing.T`; any writer failure therefore remains a genuine child failure.

This test runs in the normal gate because `make check` includes `smoke` (`Makefile:17,102-107`), and the smoke script runs the package without an allowlist (`scripts/smoke.sh:190-199`). The injected body uses no database, HTTP, or timed load and completes in seconds.

## Files touched

- `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go` — add the serialized `Partial` field.
- `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest_test.go` — extend the existing JSON metadata coverage at `:329-354` to pin the explicit `partial` key.
- `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` — add the deferred lifecycle helper; route both profiles through it; remove both terminal `writeReport` calls.
- `smoke/onsale_load_report_test.go` — add normal-return and subprocess-fatal regression tests.

## DECISION: partial marker

Options are an explicit boolean or a completion-status enum.

Recommendation: `Partial bool \`json:"partial"\``. It is the smallest additive format change and matches the ticket language. Set it `true` before entering the run and clear it only on normal return.

Trade-off: older reports omit the field, and decoding them directly into a Go `bool` yields `false`. Readers must treat a missing key as legacy/unknown—not proof of completion. A status enum would preserve that distinction automatically but adds unnecessary schema and consumer complexity for this ticket.

## Control-flow finding and risks

There is no current goroutine-exit path around the defer. `RunStage` launches workers but waits for all of them before returning (`smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:109-147`); workers return `Outcome` values and never receive `*testing.T`. All `generatorHealthy` calls and other fatal checks execute synchronously on the test goroutine.

Risks:

- `partial:false` means the profile reached its end, not that every nonfatal assertion passed; `t.Errorf` should still produce a complete report.
- `os.Exit`, `SIGKILL`, a process crash, or an unwritable report path cannot be rescued by a defer.
- The callback/helper extraction must remain synchronous; moving the profile body into a goroutine would invalidate the guarantee.
- Do not move the failed sweep append ahead of `generatorHealthy`; that would publish explicitly inconclusive evidence.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan-final — **delta** on the `kind=plan` draft. Critique by **main-agent** (`config.models.planReview`).

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Nothing restated; read the two together.

---

## 1. Existence check on every seam the draft named (`git grep` at HEAD `2fb5709`)

A drafter that cannot run the gate will hallucinate seams, so each was resolved before critique:

| Draft citation | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:474-480` — `generatorHealthy(r)` precedes the sweep append | ✅ exists, order as claimed (`:477` guard, `:478` append) |
| `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:312-329` — `type Report struct` | ✅ exists |
| `…loadtest.go:289-304` — `FinalizeP99Ms` / `ConfirmP99Ms` built in `StageResult.Report()` | ✅ exists (`:297-298`) |
| `…loadtest.go:109-147` — `RunStage` joins its workers before returning | ✅ `wg.Wait()` at `:145`; workers never receive `*testing.T` |
| `…loadtest_test.go:329-354` — `TestReportJSONCarriesRequiredMetadata` | ✅ exists, is the right place to pin the new key |
| `Makefile:17,102-107` — `check` includes `smoke` | ✅ exists |
| `scripts/smoke.sh:190-199` — package run with no `-run` allowlist | ✅ `:199` runs `go test -tags smoke -count=1 -v ./...` |
| `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:391` — `onsaleGate`'s own terminal `writeReport` | ✅ exists — same loss mode, the draft is right to catch it |

No hallucinated seam. The control-flow finding (no goroutine-exit path bypasses the defer) is
independently confirmed: `RunStage`'s workers return `Outcome` values and never touch `*testing.T`,
so every fatal in `onsaleFull` fires on the test goroutine.

## 2. Findings — accept / amend / reject

**ACCEPT — `Partial bool` with `json:"partial"`, no `omitempty`.** The draft's `DECISION:` block
recommends the boolean over a status enum; taken. Explicit `false` on complete runs is the load-
bearing part — with `omitempty` a complete run and a legacy run would both present as *absent*.
The draft's own caveat stands and is worth repeating in the code: **a missing key is legacy/unknown,
not proof of completion.** Reports written before this ticket (e.g. any TKT-82 artifact) decode to
`Partial=false` and must not be read as "verified complete".

**ACCEPT — set `true` on entry, clear only on normal return.** Fail-closed: every abnormal exit path,
named or not, leaves the report marked partial. The inverse (set `true` in the failure handler) would
require enumerating the failure paths, which is how this class of bug recurs.

**ACCEPT — `onsaleGate` gets the same treatment.** Same file, same loss mode, same schema. Cheap, and
profile-dependent reporting semantics would be a trap for the next reader. Note it is near-inert in
practice: the gate profile runs with `ONSALE_REPORT` unset, so `writeReport` returns at
`onsale_load_test.go:252` — this buys consistency, not behaviour.

**ACCEPT — the aborting stage stays out of the report.** `generatorHealthy` fires *before* the append
(`:477-478`), so a sweep stage that trips the guard is never published. That is correct and must not
be "fixed": `loadtest.CeilingInconclusive` is a **generator** verdict, and publishing an inconclusive
stage as server evidence is precisely the dishonesty the guard exists to prevent. The draft flags
this in its risks; promoting it to a DoD line.

**AMEND — the subprocess test needs a condition the draft did not state.** The draft proposes
re-executing the test binary with an env sentinel, and it is right that an expected `t.Fatal` cannot
be neutralised in-process by a subtest. But it did not check what else that child process runs: the
smoke package has a **`TestMain` at `smoke/coverage_test.go:119`** that, after `m.Run()`, enforces the
uncovered-2xx-operations coverage gate and can turn a `0` into a `1`. The child is only safe because
that gate is disarmed on filtered runs (`:122-123`: `flag.Lookup("test.run")` non-empty ⇒ skip).
**So the child MUST be invoked with a `-test.run=^…$` filter** — not merely as a convenience to
select the test, but as the thing that keeps `TestMain`'s coverage gate from firing in a child that
by construction runs one test. Without it the child's exit code stops meaning "the injected abort
happened". The parent asserts a non-zero exit, so this would not have produced a false green — but it
would have produced a green for the wrong reason, which is worse in an evidence harness.
Second condition, same area: the child test must **`t.Skip` when its sentinel env var is absent**, so
it is inert in the ordinary gate run rather than aborting it.

**AMEND — assert the abort's own evidence, not just the file's existence.** The draft's parent
assertions are right but stop short: pin that the *aborting* stage is **absent** from the written
report, alongside the completed `nfr-3000pm` stage being present with its exact injected
`finalize_p99_ms` / `confirm_p99_ms`. Presence-only assertions would still pass if a future change
started publishing inconclusive stages — the one outcome the guard exists to prevent.

**REJECT — nothing.** No part of the draft is wrong.

**NOTED, out of scope — `partial:false` means "reached the end", not "passed".** A run where a
`t.Errorf` SLO assertion failed still completes and still writes `partial:false`. The draft flags
this. I am deliberately **not** adding a second `failed` field: AC 2 asks the report to distinguish
complete from partial runs, and it does. Conflating "incomplete" with "failed" in one boolean would
make both unreadable. If a reader ever needs run-outcome in the JSON, that is a new ticket. Recording
the limitation here so it is a known boundary, not an oversight.

## 3. Decisions I made myself (Gate 2 waived — recorded per the run's terms)

Gate 2 is waived for this run **and** nominally skipped anyway by `risk:low`. Rule applied: prefer
the critique's recommendation; absent one, the most reversible option.

| # | Decision | How resolved | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Partial marker: boolean vs. status enum | **boolean `partial`** | The draft's `DECISION:` block recommends it — critique-recommended option taken as-is. Smallest additive schema change; an enum can be added later without breaking a boolean reader. |
| D2 | Abort-injection seam: subprocess re-exec vs. in-process `runtime.Goexit` in a goroutine | **subprocess re-exec** | The draft recommends it. I weighed the smaller in-process alternative (a `runtime.Goexit()` body in a goroutine — `t.FailNow` *is* `runtime.Goexit`, so it exercises the same primitive in ~⅓ the code) and rejected it: it proves the property through *my belief about* what `t.Fatalf` does, where the subprocess proves it through the real `t.Fatalf`. `AGENTS.md` names exactly this trap — a fixture built from the type under test encodes the compatibility it claims to prove. Cost is ~20 lines and one process spawn of a stack-free test. |
| D3 | Does `onsaleGate` change too, when the ticket names only `onsaleFull`? | **yes** | Draft-recommended; same file, so inside the ticket's stated scope (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go`). Reversible — it is one call site. |
| D4 | Add a `failed` field alongside `partial`? | **no** | No critique recommendation, so: most reversible = don't add schema. Adding a field later is additive; removing a published one is not. |

`risk:low` **stands** after planning: two test files plus one struct field, all under `smoke/`. No
auth, no money path, no migration, no CI/deploy config. The stop-condition for touching those was
not triggered.

## 4. Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Per the skill: design elements *added* at 3b reach the gate with only their author's eyes on them.
Named again here and in the code review focus.

1. **The `-test.run=^…$` filter on the child invocation, as a correctness requirement rather than a
   convenience** — with the reason (`TestMain`'s coverage gate at `smoke/coverage_test.go:119-127`).
   Mine; gpt-5.6-sol never saw `TestMain`.
2. **The `t.Skip`-unless-sentinel guard on the child test**, so it is inert in the ordinary gate.
   Mine.
3. **The assertion that the aborting stage is absent from the written report** (not merely that
   completed stages are present). Mine.

All three are test-only. The ai-review stage (`gpt-5.6-sol`) sees them as part of the diff, which is
the second pair of eyes they are otherwise missing — the review focus will name them explicitly.

## 5. TDD order for `agent:coding`

1. Write both tests first; run them; **observe red** — the abort-path test must fail against the
   current terminal `writeReport`, and the JSON test must fail against a `Report` with no `Partial`.
   Capture that red output; it is the evidence for AC 1 and AC 2.
2. Add `Partial` to `loadtest.Report`; add the deferred lifecycle helper; route both profiles
   through it; delete both terminal `writeReport` calls.
3. Green, then the full `make check` (run as the sole command in its shell call, exit code read from
   a file, per the skill's gate rules).

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implemented by **main-agent** (`config.models.implement`) — PR [#122](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/122), commit `84f40be`

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent
branch: TKT-130-defer-onsale-report
base: origin/main @ 2fb5709
pr: 122
commit: 84f40be
diff: +41 / -2 (3 files, 1 new)
gate: make check EXIT=0 (sentinel file), 0 failure signatures in the log body
```

### TDD — red observed first, and it was a *behavioural* red

The first red was only a compile error (`Report has no field Partial`, `undefined: beginReport`),
which proves nothing about the defect. So I added the field plus a **deliberately wrong
`beginReport` reproducing the pre-fix semantics** (write only at completion) and re-ran:

```
--- FAIL: TestOnsaleReportSurvivesAnAbortedStage (0.02s)
    aborted run wrote no report: open …/report.json: no such file or directory
    child output:
        onsale_load_report_test.go:88: injected abort at sweep-600
        --- FAIL: TestOnsaleReportSurvivesAnAbortedStage
```

That is the TKT-125 failure mode reproduced in 0.02 s — the child aborted, exited non-zero, and left
no JSON. Then the scaffold was replaced with the real `beginReport` and both tests went green. The
completion-path test passed against the scaffold, correctly: the pre-fix code did write on a clean
run; only the abort path was broken.

### What shipped

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go` | `Partial bool \`json:"partial"\`` on `Report`, no `omitempty`, with the reasoning in a comment |
| `smoke/onsale_load_test.go` | `beginReport` helper; both profiles route through it; both terminal `writeReport` calls become `complete()` |
| `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest_test.go` | pins that a complete report serializes `"partial": false` **explicitly** (guards against someone adding `omitempty`) |
| `smoke/onsale_load_report_test.go` *(new)* | the two mechanism tests |

### Deviations from `kind=plan-final`, and why

1. **`t.Cleanup` instead of `defer`.** The plan said `defer writeReport`. A `defer` *inside* a helper
   fires when the helper returns — immediately — so the returned-completion-func shape requires
   `t.Cleanup`. Same guarantee for the same reason (`FailNow` is `runtime.Goexit`; cleanups run on
   abort exactly as defers do), and it avoids reindenting ~120 lines of profile body into a closure,
   which the plan's `reportRun(t, r, func(){…})` shape would have cost. Net effect on the diff:
   4 changed lines at the call sites instead of a whole-function reindent.
2. **The child guard is an env check with an early return, not `t.Skip`.** Plan-final item 2 of
   §4 called for `t.Skip` unless the sentinel is set. One test function that dispatches on the env
   var is simpler and removes the "skipped test" noise from every ordinary gate run. Same intent,
   and it makes the parent's `-test.run=^`+`t.Name()`+`$` self-referential, so the filter can't drift
   from the test name.

Everything else is as planned. The three plan-review-only additions (§4 of `kind=plan-final`) all
shipped and are in the diff the reviewer sees: the load-bearing `-test.run` filter, the child guard,
and the assertion that the aborting stage is **absent** from the report.

### `risk:low` after implementation

**Stands.** 3 files, all under `smoke/`, test-harness only. No auth, no money path, no migration, no
CI/deploy config — none of the run's stop conditions were triggered.
